verses.original: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ἀνέδειξεν ὁ Κύριος καὶ ἑτέρους ἑβδομήκοντα δύο καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς ἀνὰ δύο δύο πρὸ προσώπου αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν πόλιν καὶ τόπον οὗ ἤμελλεν αὐτὸς ἔρχεσθαι
verses.transliteration: Meta de tauta anedeixen ho Kyrios kai heterous hebdomēkonta dyo kai apesteilen autous ana dyo dyo pro prosōpou autou eis pasan polin kai topon hou ēmellen autos erchesthai
verses.literal: After this the Lord appointed seventy-two . . . others and sent them two by two . . . ahead of Him . . . . . . to every town and place . . . He was about to visit
verses.literalPt: Depois disso, o Senhor designou outros setenta e enviou-os de dois em dois adiante de si a todas as cidades e lugares aonde ele estava para ir.

verses.original: ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Ὁ μὲν θερισμὸς πολύς οἱ δὲ ἐργάται ὀλίγοι δεήθητε οὖν τοῦ Κυρίου τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὅπως ἐργάτας ἐκβάλῃ εἰς τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: elegen de pros autous Ho men therismos polys hoi de ergatai oligoi deēthēte oun tou Kyriou tou therismou hopōs ergatas ekbalē eis ton therismon autou
verses.literal: And He told . . . them The harvest is plentiful but the workers are few Ask the Lord of the harvest therefore to send out workers into His harvest
verses.literalPt: Disse-lhes: A seara, na verdade, é grande, mas os trabalhadores são poucos; rogai, pois, ao senhor da seara que envie trabalhadores para a sua seara.

verses.original: Ὑπάγετε ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω ὑμᾶς ὡς ἄρνας ἐν μέσῳ λύκων
verses.transliteration: Hypagete idou apostellō hymas hōs arnas en mesō lykōn
verses.literal: Go . . . I am sending you out . . . like lambs among wolves
verses.literalPt: Ide; eu vos envio como cordeiros no meio de lobos.

verses.original: μὴ βαστάζετε βαλλάντιον μὴ πήραν μὴ ὑποδήματα καὶ μηδένα κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἀσπάσησθε
verses.transliteration: mē bastazete ballantion mē pēran mē hypodēmata kai mēdena kata tēn hodon aspasēsthe
verses.literal: Carry no purse or bag or sandals Do not greet anyone along the road
verses.literalPt: Não leveis bolsa, nem alforje, nem sandálias; e a ninguém saudeis pelo caminho.

verses.original: Εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν εἰσέλθητε οἰκίαν πρῶτον λέγετε Εἰρήνη τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ
verses.transliteration: Eis hēn d’ an eiselthēte oikian prōton legete Eirēnē tō oikō toutō
verses.literal: Whatever . . . house you enter . . . begin by saying Peace to this house
verses.literalPt: Em qualquer casa em que entrardes, dizei primeiro: Paz seja nesta casa!

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἐκεῖ ᾖ υἱὸς εἰρήνης ἐπαναπαήσεται ἐπ’ αὐτὸν ἡ εἰρήνη ὑμῶν εἰ δὲ μή¦γε ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἀνακάμψει
verses.transliteration: kai ean ekei ē huios eirēnēs epanapaēsetai ep’ auton hē eirēnē hymōn ei de mē¦ge eph’ hymas anakampsei
verses.literal: If a man of peace is there your peace will rest on him if not it will return to you
verses.literalPt: Se ali houver algum filho da paz, repousará sobre ele a vossa paz; e, se não houver, ela tornará para vós.

verses.original: ἐν αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένετε ἐσθίοντες καὶ πίνοντες τὰ παρ’ αὐτῶν ἄξιος γὰρ ὁ ἐργάτης τοῦ μισθοῦ αὐτοῦ μὴ μεταβαίνετε ἐξ οἰκίας εἰς οἰκίαν
verses.transliteration: en autē de tē oikia menete esthiontes kai pinontes ta par’ autōn axios gar ho ergatēs tou misthou autou mē metabainete ex oikias eis oikian
verses.literal: Stay at the same house eating and drinking whatever you are offered . . . . . . For the worker is worthy of his wages Do not move around from house to house
verses.literalPt: Permanecei naquela mesma casa, comendo e bebendo o que vos oferecerem; pois digno é o trabalhador do seu salário. Não vos mudeis de casa em casa.

verses.original: Καὶ εἰς ἣν ἂν πόλιν εἰσέρχησθε καὶ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς ἐσθίετε τὰ παρατιθέμενα ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: Kai eis hēn an polin eiserchēsthe kai dechōntai hymas esthiete ta paratithemena hymin
verses.literal: If you enter . . . a town and they welcome you eat whatever is set before you
verses.literalPt: Em qualquer cidade em que entrardes e vos receberem, comei o que vos oferecerem;

verses.original: καὶ θεραπεύετε τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ ἀσθενεῖς καὶ λέγετε αὐτοῖς Ἤγγικεν ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai therapeuete tous en autē astheneis kai legete autois Ēngiken eph’ hymas hē basileia tou Theou
verses.literal: Heal the sick who are there and tell them The kingdom of God is near you
verses.literalPt: curai os enfermos que nela houver e dizei: Está próximo a vós o reino de Deus.

verses.original: Εἰς ἣν δ’ ἂν πόλιν εἰσέλθητε καὶ μὴ δέχωνται ὑμᾶς ἐξελθόντες εἰς τὰς πλατείας αὐτῆς εἴπατε
verses.transliteration: Eis hēn d’ an polin eiselthēte kai mē dechōntai hymas exelthontes eis tas plateias autēs eipate
verses.literal: But if you enter . . . a . . . town and they do not welcome you go into the streets and declare
verses.literalPt: Mas, na cidade em que entrardes e não vos receberem, saindo pelas suas ruas, dizei:

verses.original: Καὶ τὸν κονιορτὸν τὸν κολληθέντα ἡμῖν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ὑμῶν εἰς τοὺς πόδας ἀπομασσόμεθα ὑμῖν πλὴν τοῦτο γινώσκετε ὅτι ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai ton koniorton ton kollēthenta hēmin ek tēs poleōs hymōn eis tous podas apomassometha hymin plēn touto ginōskete hoti ēngiken hē basileia tou Theou
verses.literal: Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet we wipe off as a testimony against you Yet be sure of this The kingdom of God is near
verses.literalPt: Até o pó que da vossa cidade se nos pegou aos pés sacudimos contra vós; todavia, sabei que está próximo o reino de Deus.

verses.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι Σοδόμοις ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἢ τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ
verses.transliteration: legō hymin hoti Sodomois en tē hēmera ekeinē anektoteron estai ē tē polei ekeinē
verses.literal: I tell you it will be more bearable on that day for Sodom than for that town
verses.literalPt: Digo-vos que, naquele dia, haverá menos rigor para Sodoma do que para aquela cidade.

verses.original: Οὐαί σοι Χοραζίν οὐαί σοι Βηθσαϊδά ὅτι εἰ ἐν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἐγενήθησαν αἱ δυνάμεις αἱ γενόμεναι ἐν ὑμῖν πάλαι ἂν ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ καθήμενοι μετενόησαν
verses.transliteration: Ouai soi Chorazin ouai soi Bēthsaida hoti ei en Tyrō kai Sidōni egenēthēsan hai dynameis hai genomenai en hymin palai an en sakkō kai spodō kathēmenoi metenoēsan
verses.literal: Woe to you Chorazin Woe to you Bethsaida For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon they would have repented long ago sitting in sackcloth and ashes
verses.literalPt: Ai de ti, Corazim! Ai de ti, Betsaida! Porque, se em Tiro e em Sidom se tivessem operado os milagres que em vós se fizeram, há muito, sentadas em saco e em cinza, elas se teriam arrependido.

verses.original: πλὴν Τύρῳ καὶ Σιδῶνι ἀνεκτότερον ἔσται ἐν τῇ κρίσει ἢ ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: plēn Tyrō kai Sidōni anektoteron estai en tē krisei ē hymin
verses.literal: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you
verses.literalPt: Contudo, haverá menos rigor para Tiro e para Sidom no dia do juízo, do que para vós.

verses.original: καὶ σύ Καφαρναούμ μὴ ἕως οὐρανοῦ ὑψωθήσῃ ἕως τοῦ ᾅδου καταβήσῃ
verses.transliteration: kai sy Kapharnaoum mē heōs ouranou hypsōthēsē heōs tou hadou katabēsē
verses.literal: And you Capernaum will you be lifted up to heaven No you will be brought down to Hades
verses.literalPt: Tu, Cafarnaum, elevar-te-ás, porventura, até o céu? Descerás até o Hades.

verses.original: Ὁ ἀκούων ὑμῶν ἐμοῦ ἀκούει καὶ ὁ ἀθετῶν ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ ἀθετεῖ ὁ δὲ ἐμὲ ἀθετῶν ἀθετεῖ τὸν ἀποστείλαντά με
verses.transliteration: Ho akouōn hymōn emou akouei kai ho athetōn hymas eme athetei ho de eme athetōn athetei ton aposteilanta me
verses.literal: Whoever listens to you listens to Me whoever rejects you rejects Me and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me
verses.literalPt: Quem vos ouve a mim me ouve; quem vos rejeita a mim me rejeita; e quem me rejeita rejeita aquele que me enviou.

verses.original: Ὑπέστρεψαν δὲ οἱ ἑβδομήκοντα δύο μετὰ χαρᾶς λέγοντες Κύριε καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ὑποτάσσεται ἡμῖν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου
verses.transliteration: Hypestrepsan de hoi hebdomēkonta dyo meta charas legontes Kyrie kai ta daimonia hypotassetai hēmin en tō onomati sou
verses.literal: The seventy-two . . . returned with joy and said Lord even the demons submit to us in Your name
verses.literalPt: Voltaram os setenta, cheios de alegria, dizendo: Senhor, até os demônios se nos submetem em teu nome.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς Ἐθεώρουν τὸν Σατανᾶν ὡς ἀστραπὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ πεσόντα
verses.transliteration: Eipen de autois Etheōroun ton Satanan hōs astrapēn ek tou ouranou pesonta
verses.literal: So He told them I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven
verses.literalPt: Respondeu-lhes Jesus: Eu via a Satanás cair do céu como relâmpago.

verses.original: ἰδοὺ δέδωκα ὑμῖν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πατεῖν ἐπάνω ὄφεων καὶ σκορπίων καὶ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ἐχθροῦ καὶ οὐδὲν ὑμᾶς οὐ μὴ ἀδικήσῃ
verses.transliteration: idou dedōka hymin tēn exousian tou patein epanō opheōn kai skorpiōn kai epi pasan tēn dynamin tou echthrou kai ouden hymas ou mē adikēsē
verses.literal: Behold I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy Nothing . . . . . . will harm you
verses.literalPt: Eis aí vos dei autoridade para pisardes serpentes e escorpiões e sobre todo o poder do inimigo, e nada de modo algum vos fará mal.

verses.original: πλὴν ἐν τούτῳ μὴ χαίρετε ὅτι τὰ πνεύματα ὑμῖν ὑποτάσσεται χαίρετε δὲ ὅτι τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν ἐνγέγραπται ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς
verses.transliteration: plēn en toutō mē chairete hoti ta pneumata hymin hypotassetai chairete de hoti ta onomata hymōn engegraptai en tois ouranois
verses.literal: Nevertheless do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you but rejoice that your names are written in heaven
verses.literalPt: Mas não vos regozijeis em que os espíritos se vos submetem; antes, regozijai-vos em que os vossos nomes estão escritos no céu.

verses.original: Ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἠγαλλιάσατο ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι τῷ Ἁγίῳ καὶ εἶπεν Ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι Πάτερ Κύριε τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ τῆς γῆς ὅτι ἀπέκρυψας ταῦτα ἀπὸ σοφῶν καὶ συνετῶν καὶ ἀπεκάλυψας αὐτὰ νηπίοις ναί ὁ Πατήρ ὅτι οὕτως εὐδοκία ἐγένετο ἔμπροσθέν σου
verses.transliteration: En autē tē hōra ēgalliasato en tō Pneumati tō Hagiō kai eipen Exomologoumai soi Pater Kyrie tou ouranou kai tēs gēs hoti apekrypsas tauta apo sophōn kai synetōn kai apekalypsas auta nēpiois nai ho Patēr hoti houtōs eudokia egeneto emprosthen sou
verses.literal: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared I praise You Father Lord of heaven and earth because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned and revealed them to little children Yes Father for this was well-pleasing in Your sight . . .
verses.literalPt: Naquela hora, exultou Jesus no Espírito Santo e exclamou: Graças te dou a ti, Pai, Senhor do céu e da terra, porque escondeste essas coisas aos sábios e entendidos e as revelaste aos pequeninos! Assim é, Pai, porque assim foi do teu agrado.

verses.original: Πάντα μοι παρεδόθη ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου καὶ οὐδεὶς γινώσκει τίς ἐστιν ὁ Υἱὸς εἰ μὴ ὁ Πατήρ καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ Πατὴρ εἰ μὴ ὁ Υἱὸς καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν βούληται ὁ Υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψαι
verses.transliteration: Panta moi paredothē hypo tou Patros mou kai oudeis ginōskei tis estin ho Huios ei mē ho Patēr kai tis estin ho Patēr ei mē ho Huios kai hō ean boulētai ho Huios apokalypsai
verses.literal: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father No one knows who the Son is except . . . the Father and no one knows who the Father is except . . . the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him
verses.literalPt: Todas as coisas me foram entregues por meu Pai. Ninguém sabe quem é o Filho, senão o Pai; nem quem é o Pai, senão o Filho, e aquele a quem o Filho o quiser revelar.

verses.original: Καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς κατ’ ἰδίαν εἶπεν Μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ οἱ βλέποντες ἃ βλέπετε
verses.transliteration: Kai strapheis pros tous mathētas kat’ idian eipen Makarioi hoi ophthalmoi hoi blepontes ha blepete
verses.literal: Then Jesus turned to the disciples and said privately Blessed are the eyes that see what you see
verses.literalPt: Virando-se para seus discípulos, disse-lhes em particular: Ditosos os olhos que veem o que vós vedes.

verses.original: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ βασιλεῖς ἠθέλησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ ὑμεῖς βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν
verses.transliteration: legō gar hymin hoti polloi prophētai kai basileis ēthelēsan idein ha hymeis blepete kai ouk eidan kai akousai ha akouete kai ouk ēkousan
verses.literal: For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it and to hear what you hear but did not hear it
verses.literalPt: Pois vos digo que muitos profetas e reis desejaram ver o que vedes e não no viram; e ouvir o que ouvis e não no ouviram.

verses.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ νομικός τις ἀνέστη ἐκπειράζων αὐτὸν λέγων Διδάσκαλε τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω
verses.transliteration: Kai idou nomikos tis anestē ekpeirazōn auton legōn Didaskale ti poiēsas zōēn aiōnion klēronomēsō
verses.literal: One day . . . an expert in the law stood up to test Him Teacher he asked what must I do to inherit eternal life
verses.literalPt: Levantando-se um doutor da lei, experimentou-o, dizendo: Mestre, que farei para herdar a vida eterna?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Ἐν τῷ νόμῳ τί γέγραπται πῶς ἀναγινώσκεις
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen pros auton En tō nomō ti gegraptai pōs anaginōskeis
verses.literal: What is written in the Law - Jesus replied - How do you read it
verses.literalPt: Respondeu-lhe Jesus: Que é o que está escrito na lei? Como lês tu?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Ἀγαπήσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ἰσχύϊ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου καὶ Τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν
verses.transliteration: Ho de apokritheis eipen Agapēseis Kyrion ton Theon sou ex holēs tēs kardias sou kai en holē tē psychē sou kai en holē tē ischui sou kai en holē tē dianoia sou kai Ton plēsion sou hōs seauton
verses.literal: He answered Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind and Love your neighbor as yourself
verses.literalPt: Respondeu ele: Amarás o Senhor, teu Deus, de todo o teu coração, de toda a tua alma, de toda a tua força e de todo o teu entendimento, e o teu próximo como a ti mesmo.

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Ὀρθῶς ἀπεκρίθης τοῦτο ποίει καὶ ζήσῃ
verses.transliteration: Eipen de autō Orthōs apekrithēs touto poiei kai zēsē
verses.literal: You have answered correctly Jesus said . . . Do this and you will live
verses.literalPt: Replicou-lhe Jesus: Respondeste bem; faze isso e viverás.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ θέλων δικαιῶσαι ἑαυτὸν εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν Καὶ τίς ἐστίν μου πλησίον
verses.transliteration: Ho de thelōn dikaiōsai heauton eipen pros ton Iēsoun Kai tis estin mou plēsion
verses.literal: But wanting to justify himself he asked - Jesus And who is my neighbor
verses.literalPt: Ele, porém, querendo justificar-se, perguntou a Jesus: E quem é o meu próximo?

verses.original: Ὑπολαβὼν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ἄνθρωπός τις κατέβαινεν ἀπὸ Ἰερουσαλὴμ εἰς Ἰεριχὼ καὶ λῃσταῖς περιέπεσεν οἳ καὶ ἐκδύσαντες αὐτὸν καὶ πληγὰς ἐπιθέντες ἀπῆλθον ἀφέντες ἡμιθανῆ
verses.transliteration: Hypolabōn de ho Iēsous eipen Anthrōpos tis katebainen apo Ierousalēm eis Ierichō kai lēstais periepesen hoi kai ekdysantes auton kai plēgas epithentes apēlthon aphentes hēmithanē
verses.literal: Jesus took up this question and said A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers They stripped him beat . . . him and went away leaving him half dead
verses.literalPt: Prosseguindo Jesus, disse: Um homem descia de Jerusalém a Jericó e caiu nas mãos de salteadores, que, depois de o despirem e espancarem, se retiraram, deixando-o meio morto.

verses.original: Κατὰ συγκυρίαν δὲ ἱερεύς τις κατέβαινεν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν
verses.transliteration: Kata synkyrian de hiereus tis katebainen en tē hodō ekeinē kai idōn auton antiparēlthen
verses.literal: Now by chance a priest was going down . . . the same road but when he saw him he passed by on the other side
verses.literalPt: Por uma coincidência, descia por aquele caminho um sacerdote; quando o viu, passou de largo.

verses.original: Ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Λευίτης γενόμενος κατὰ τὸν τόπον ἐλθὼν καὶ ἰδὼν ἀντιπαρῆλθεν
verses.transliteration: Homoiōs de kai Leuitēs genomenos kata ton topon elthōn kai idōn antiparēlthen
verses.literal: So too when a Levite came to that spot and saw him he passed by on the other side
verses.literalPt: Do mesmo modo, também um levita, chegando ao lugar e vendo-o, passou de largo.

verses.original: Σαμαρίτης δέ τις ὁδεύων ἦλθεν κατ’ αὐτὸν καὶ ἰδὼν ἐσπλαγχνίσθη
verses.transliteration: Samaritēs de tis hodeuōn ēlthen kat’ auton kai idōn esplanchnisthē
verses.literal: But a Samaritan on a journey came upon him and when he saw him he had compassion
verses.literalPt: Um samaritano, porém, que ia de viagem, aproximou-se do homem e, vendo-o, teve compaixão dele.

verses.original: καὶ προσελθὼν κατέδησεν τὰ τραύματα αὐτοῦ ἐπιχέων ἔλαιον καὶ οἶνον ἐπιβιβάσας δὲ αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ ἴδιον κτῆνος ἤγαγεν αὐτὸν εἰς πανδοχεῖον καὶ ἐπεμελήθη αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai proselthōn katedēsen ta traumata autou epicheōn elaion kai oinon epibibasas de auton epi to idion ktēnos ēgagen auton eis pandocheion kai epemelēthē autou
verses.literal: He went to him and bandaged his wounds pouring on oil and wine Then he put him on his own animal brought him to an inn and took care of him
verses.literalPt: Chegando-se, atou-lhe as feridas, deitando nelas azeite e vinho; e, pondo-o sobre o seu animal, levou-o para uma hospedaria e tratou-o.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον ἐκβαλὼν δύο δηνάρια ἔδωκεν τῷ πανδοχεῖ καὶ εἶπεν Ἐπιμελήθητι αὐτοῦ καὶ ὅ τι ἂν προσδαπανήσῃς ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ ἐπανέρχεσθαί με ἀποδώσω σοι
verses.transliteration: Kai epi tēn aurion ekbalōn dyo dēnaria edōken tō pandochei kai eipen Epimelēthēti autou kai ho ti an prosdapanēsēs egō en tō epanerchesthai me apodōsō soi
verses.literal: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper Take care of him he said and on my return I will repay you for any additional . . . . . . expense
verses.literalPt: No dia seguinte, tirou dois denários, deu-os ao hospedeiro e disse: Trata-o e quanto gastares de mais, na volta eu to pagarei.

verses.original: Τίς τούτων τῶν τριῶν πλησίον δοκεῖ σοι γεγονέναι τοῦ ἐμπεσόντος εἰς τοὺς λῃστάς
verses.transliteration: Tis toutōn tōn triōn plēsion dokei soi gegonenai tou empesontos eis tous lēstas
verses.literal: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers
verses.literalPt: Qual desses três te parece ter sido o próximo daquele que caiu nas mãos dos salteadores?

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ὁ ποιήσας τὸ ἔλεος μετ’ αὐτοῦ Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πορεύου καὶ σὺ ποίει ὁμοίως
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen Ho poiēsas to eleos met’ autou Eipen de autō ho Iēsous Poreuou kai sy poiei homoiōs
verses.literal: The one who showed . . . him mercy - replied the expert in the law Then Jesus told him Go and do likewise
verses.literalPt: Respondeu o doutor da lei: Aquele que usou de misericórdia para com ele. Disse-lhe Jesus: Vai-te e faze tu o mesmo.

verses.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι αὐτοὺς αὐτὸς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς κώμην τινά γυνὴ δέ τις ὀνόματι Μάρθα ὑπεδέξατο αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν
verses.transliteration: En de tō poreuesthai autous autos eisēlthen eis kōmēn tina gynē de tis onomati Martha hypedexato auton eis tēn oikian
verses.literal: As . . . they traveled along Jesus entered . . . a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home
verses.literalPt: Quando iam de caminho, entrou ele em uma aldeia; e uma mulher chamada Marta hospedou-o.

verses.original: καὶ τῇδε ἦν ἀδελφὴ καλουμένη Μαριάμ ἣ καὶ παρακαθεσθεῖσα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας τοῦ Κυρίου ἤκουεν τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai tēde ēn adelphē kaloumenē Mariam hē kai parakathestheisa pros tous podas tou Kyriou ēkouen ton logon autou
verses.literal: She had a sister named Mary who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message
verses.literalPt: Esta tinha uma irmã chamada Maria, a qual, sentada aos pés do Senhor, ouvia o seu ensino.

verses.original: ἡ δὲ Μάρθα περιεσπᾶτο περὶ πολλὴν διακονίαν ἐπιστᾶσα δὲ εἶπεν Κύριε οὐ μέλει σοι ὅτι ἡ ἀδελφή μου μόνην με κατέλειπεν διακονεῖν εἰπὲ οὖν αὐτῇ ἵνα μοι συναντιλάβηται
verses.transliteration: hē de Martha periespato peri pollēn diakonian epistasa de eipen Kyrie ou melei soi hoti hē adelphē mou monēn me kateleipen diakonein eipe oun autē hina moi synantilabētai
verses.literal: But Martha was distracted by all the . . . preparations to be made She came to Jesus and said Lord do You not care . . . that my sister has left me to serve alone Tell her to help me
verses.literalPt: Marta, porém, andava preocupada com muito serviço; e, chegando-se, disse: Senhor, a ti não se te dá que minha irmã me tenha deixado só a servir? Manda-lhe, pois, que me ajude.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ ὁ Κύριος Μάρθα Μάρθα μεριμνᾷς καὶ θορυβάζῃ περὶ πολλά
verses.transliteration: Apokritheis de eipen autē ho Kyrios Martha Martha merimnas kai thorybazē peri polla
verses.literal: Martha Martha the Lord replied - you are worried and upset about many things
verses.literalPt: Mas respondeu-lhe o Senhor: Marta, Marta, estás ansiosa e te ocupas com muitas coisas.

verses.original: ὀλίγων δέ ἐστιν χρεία ἢ ἑνός Μαριὰμ γὰρ τὴν ἀγαθὴν μερίδα ἐξελέξατο ἥτις οὐκ ἀφαιρεθήσεται αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: oligōn de estin chreia ē henos Mariam gar tēn agathēn merida exelexato hētis ouk aphairethēsetai autēs
verses.literal: But only one thing is necessary Mary has chosen the good portion and it will not be taken away from her
verses.literalPt: Entretanto, poucas são necessárias ou, antes, uma só. Maria escolheu a boa parte, que não lhe será tirada.
